chronology_evidence_for_timing: SEC submissions metadata for the Jan 1 - Mar 31, 2026 window contains only the target 8-K and a same-day 10-K; both acceptance timestamps (12:10:10 UTC and 20:52:00 UTC) are AFTER the 08:02 ET wire minute, so neither is an earlier disclosure channel.
Four December 2025 SEC filings (two Form 4s, two 8-Ks for personnel/severance matters) were individually read; none announces or references Q4/FY2025 results.

Solesence's own investor-relations news archive (ir.solesence.com) was paged through for all of 2026 and the boundary into 2025: a Feb 26 executive-appointment release and a Mar 19 call-notice release (schedules the Mar 31 premarket release and 08:30 ET call, contains no results) are the only entries before the target release. The most recent 2025 entry is a Nov 11 Q3 2025 results release -- a different, earlier quarter.

The January 8, 2026 BeautyMatter/Solesence webinar ('The SPF Advantage') was investigated to exhaustion: confirmed topic is SPF product-development strategy (not earnings) via the event's own landing page; no recording or transcript found via search; the webinar is not listed in Solesence's own webinar archive at all; the one article that looked like related coverage was from 2020 and unrelated (a false lead, caught before being relied on).
No evidence of any other conference, analyst call, or public presentation between Jan 1 and Mar 31, 2026 was found despite multiple search passes across sessions.
chronology_gap_that_cannot_be_closed_by_: Open-web research can show no discoverable earlier disclosure; it cannot prove a negative for something that may have been said live and unrecorded (e.g. at an unindexed investor meeting) with zero public trace. This is the residual, irreducible uncertainty a human sign-off is being asked to accept, not a gap more searching would close.
identity_evidence: Both December 2025 8-K cover pages identify SLSN on Nasdaq as common stock, consistent with the March 2026 target filing.
No ticker change, merger, or reused-symbol event found in this window.
Not independently checked against a primary security-master/CUSIP source beyond SEC filing covers themselves.

provider_rights_status.summary: Read Alpaca's Terms and Conditions and a representative NASDAQ Global Subscriber Agreement in full. As a Non-Professional Subscriber, Information is licensed for personal use, which this project fits. The harder question: the NASDAQ agreement's definition of 'Information' extends to derived data that can be 'recalculated or re-engineered' back to the original, or that 'can be used as a substitute for' the original. Bare return percentages and booleans (no anchor price, which this project already redacts) cannot be reverse-engineered to specific quoted prices -- this appears to hold up. The genuinely open question is whether the AGGREGATE of derived labels across the full 100+-event target could eventually look like a substitute data product; that is not resolved by more reading, it is a judgment call, the same shape as the timing and corporate-action gaps but with contractual rather than evidentiary stakes.
provider_rights_status.why_this_is_the_highest_stakes_of_the_th: Timing and corporate-action sign-offs are about evidentiary sufficiency for a research claim. This one is about contractual compliance with a third party's terms. Getting it wrong has different consequences than an under-evidenced timestamp.
provider_rights_status.awaiting: An explicit sign-off from the project owner specifically authorizing provider.research_permitted:true for this use, understanding the 'substitute for Information' question is not fully closed, particularly at scale.
